articles.title: No Boss, No Money: The Raw Reality of a Chinese Gen-Z Freelancer
articles.excerpt: Jared is 28. He used to be an AI algorithm engineer at one of China's big tech firms — the kind of job millions compete for. He quit because he could not stand the 996 schedule: 9 a.m. to 9 p.m., six…
articles.body: Jared is 28. He used to be an AI algorithm engineer at one of China's big tech firms — the kind of job millions compete for. He quit because he could not stand the 996 schedule: 9 a.m. to 9 p.m., six days a week. He traded the "iron rice bowl" for freelance work, and his life now, documented by the channel Inside China Lives, is a clear-eyed look at what that freedom actually costs. He and his wife, married a year, live in an illegal rooftop structure on top of a 1990s apartment block. No proper title, no formal lease — they pay rent each month to the landlord downstairs. They have lived there three years. The rooftop bakes in summer, and the landlord will not install air conditioning. So Jared built his own cooling: a high-pressure electric misting system.
articles.author: doogee “doogeetop” top

articles.title: How to Generate Beautiful Code Screenshots 100% Client-Side (No Server Uploads, Zero Telemetry)
articles.excerpt: If you've ever shared code snippets on Twitter/X, LinkedIn, tech blogs, or team documentation, you've probably used snippet beautifiers like Carbon or Ray.so. They turn plain code blocks into aestheti…
articles.body: If you've ever shared code snippets on Twitter/X, LinkedIn, tech blogs, or team documentation, you've probably used snippet beautifiers like Carbon or Ray.so. They turn plain code blocks into aesthetically pleasing images with macOS-style window frames and modern gradient backgrounds. However, there is an uncomfortable reality when working with proprietary codebases, internal APIs, or sensitive algorithms: many web converters send keystrokes and code strings to backend APIs or third-party telemetry services . If your snippet contains internal function names, database schema fragments, or accidental environment variables, pasting it into a cloud-rendered tool is a compliance risk.

articles.excerpt: Disclosure: I'm the developer of Bolo, the app this code comes from, and this post is published from my account. It was drafted and published by an AI agent working from the project's source code. Bol…
articles.body: Disclosure: I'm the developer of Bolo, the app this code comes from, and this post is published from my account. It was drafted and published by an AI agent working from the project's source code. Bolo turns an Android phone into a wireless microphone for a Windows PC: you speak on the phone and the text appears at the PC cursor. Before any of that, the phone has to find the PC on the Wi-Fi without anyone typing an IP address. This post is about the one setup where my first discovery design quietly failed, a Windows PC shared by several signed-in users, and the small file-based fix. Two discovery paths, because one is not enough The Windows helper advertises itself two ways: mDNS / DNS-SD as _bolo._tcp , with the PC name, user name and a stable serverId in the TXT record.

articles.title: Turn a Lighthouse export into tickets with traceable threshold evidence
articles.excerpt: A performance backlog becomes difficult to maintain when a ticket says only that a page is slow. The developer needs the measured value, the device strategy, the source capture time and the rule that…
articles.body: A performance backlog becomes difficult to maintain when a ticket says only that a page is slow. The developer needs the measured value, the device strategy, the source capture time and the rule that made the issue actionable. Without those fields, a later audit can appear to contradict the ticket even though it measured a different page state. PageSpeed Remediation Backlog Builder processes an existing audit batch. It accepts compatible normalized rows and native Lighthouse result objects, then produces a report for each usable URL and strategy pair. Collection remains a separate step. This makes the transformation useful when a team already has a PageSpeed export and wants an inspectable engineering queue.

articles.body: A module-level cache can reuse completed data across requests in a Cloudflare Worker. Sharing a pending operation is a different decision: the work behind that promise may belong to the request that started it. Our rule for Teasa's isolate caches is to share completed values and let concurrent misses perform their own reads. This article explains that tradeoff, provides a small JavaScript implementation, and tests the case that ordinary cache-hit tests miss: request A's read never completes, but request B still needs an answer. Relaymote is unofficial; not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic. Relaymote (MIT, Node.js) is a phone remote for Claude Desktop's Code-tab sessions. A few of its jobs are plain UI automation on the desktop: moving a session into a sidebar group, renaming a session. Before any of that runs, an idle gate checks that nobody is using the keyboard or mouse, because automation typing into a window you are using is worse than no automation. articles.body: SpaceX launched its newest batch of Starlink broadband internet satellites today (Oct. 23) from the California coast. The spacecraft, Starlink Group 15-15, were stacked 27 high inside the payload fairing of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket , which lifted off from Pad 4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base at 6:48 p.m. EDT (2248 GMT; 3:48 p.m. local time in California). The rocket's first stage booster, designated B1063, executed its main engine cutoff and stage separation about 2.5 minutes into flight, sending the second stage to continue onward to low Earth orbit (LEO). articles.body: 7 Min Read NASA, Partners Accelerate Lander Development for 2028 Moon Missions As NASA returns humans to the lunar surface and establishes a long-term presence on our closest celestial neighbor, the agency and commercial human landing system providers Blue Origin and SpaceX have streamlined the designs and changed both concepts of operations for its future crewed landers. Since NASA established initial contracts with Blue Origin and SpaceX for crewed missions to the Moon, the agency has redefined Artemis III to demonstrate rendezvous and docking capabilities between test versions of landers from each provider and the agency’s Orion spacecraft in low Earth orbit next year.

articles.title: NASA’s Artemis III Mission to Test Future Moon Lander Operations
articles.excerpt: Before astronauts return to the lunar surface, NASA will first conduct one of the most ambitious and complex test missions in the agency’s history. Launching in 2027, Artemis III will send NASA astron…
articles.body: Before astronauts return to the lunar surface, NASA will first conduct one of the most ambitious and complex test missions in the agency’s history.  Launching in 2027, Artemis III will send NASA astronauts Randy Bresnik, Frank Rubio, Andre Douglas, and ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Luca Parmitano aboard the Orion spacecraft into low Earth orbit to perform a series of demonstrations with test versions, or test articles, of human landing systems being developed by industry partners Blue Origin and SpaceX. During the planned 14-day mission, crews and flight controllers will practice the rendezvous, docking, habitation, and operational procedures that will be essential when Artemis astronauts begin landing near the Moon’s South Pole in 2028.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 23, 2007: NASA launches Harmony module to ISS on STS-120 space shuttle mission
articles.excerpt: On October 23, 2007, the space shuttle Discovery launched the Harmony module to the International Space Station. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On October 23, 2007, the space shuttle Discovery launched the Harmony module to the International Space Station . The Harmony module is a utility hub 14 feet wide and 24 feet long, or about the length of a minibus. It joins the European Space Agency's Columbus module and Japan's Kibo laboratory and serves as the crew quarters for the American astronauts. Once it was installed, the space station grew from about the size of a three-bedroom house to something more like a five-bedroom house. When astronauts delivered Harmony to the space station , they left it temporarily attached to the Unity node. After the shuttle left, astronauts used the space station's robotic arm to move the shuttle docking port out of the way at the Destiny module.
